auditor_version: Commerce schema contract and frozen v3.1 case contracts, v3.3 scoring

evidence: The half-open 2024 interval, sum of sessions, and grouping by calendar month and traffic source match the contract.
The query filters 2025 ship dates, averages per-shipment delivery minus ship date with NULL delivery dates excluded, and separately counts missing deliveries by ship month.
Returns have one row per non-null return_id, so counting that key matches the requested return records for each month in 2025.
The query divides net item revenue by distinct delivered orders with line items in each calendar month of 2025.
The 2024 signup interval, exact age and city filters, and many-to-one ZIP lookup preserve one counted row per customer.
The query filters non-NULL return reasons in calendar 2024 and groups refund_amount by reason.
The query counts one row per order for the exact paid_search, mobile and 2025 population.
The query ranks the listed products.cogs field descending and breaks ties by ascending product ID. The repository ranking validation rejected this equivalent source expression before execution.
The query groups by the catalog products segment rather than the segment recorded for each inventory snapshot row.
The query uses the return_date scope in 2025 and sums return quantity by the destination city reached through order ZIP.
The query sums return_quantity by product for the full 2023?2025 interval with no year grouping.
The requested breakdown is by payments.payment_method on payment fact rows. The query groups by orders.payment_method, which can disagree with the recorded payment method.
The shipment date is restricted to 2025, the city is the order destination, and AVG and COUNT both use recorded non-NULL fees.
The query uses the current catalog category and filters stockout_flag before grouping, so both label provenance and retention of zero-count categories differ from the contract.
The query returns individual observations across a period and omits the inner intersection of products, before/after balances, and after-minus-before delta.
The half-open range and per-snapshot grouping preserve the requested dates and prevent cross-date summation. The catalog join is many-to-one through the inventory product foreign key.
